function.title: What is a Function?
function.intro: A function is a special relationship between inputs and outputs where each input has exactly one output.
function.discovery: Let's discover what makes functions so special! Imagine you're at a vending machine...
function.keyRule: Every input must produce exactly ONE output. Think of it like a vending machine: you press one button (input) and get one specific snack (output).
function.example1: 🏫 Your student ID number → Your name (each ID matches exactly one student)
function.example2: 🗓️ Today's date → Temperature at noon (each day has one temperature at that time)
function.example3: 🚗 Miles driven → Gallons of gas used (for each distance, there's one amount of gas needed)
function.example4: 🎮 Hours of gaming → Your score (each time period produces one score)

notation.title: Function Notation
notation.explanation: Function notation is a mathematical shorthand for describing functions. It looks like this:
notation.part1: f is the name of the function (like a nickname)
notation.part2: x is the input variable (what goes in)
notation.part3: f(x) means "the output of function f when the input is x"
notation.example1: means "the value of f when x is 5"
notation.example2: is a different function named g
notation.example3: means "the value of h when the input is 3"

domainRange.title: Domain and Range
domainRange.domainExample: Think of it as all the buttons on your vending machine.
domainRange.rangeExample: Think of it as all the snacks that can come out of the machine.
domainRange.analogyContent: The domain is all the button numbers you can press (like A1, A2, B1, etc.). The range is all the different snacks you can get out.

representations.title: Ways to Represent Functions
representations.intro: Functions can be shown in four different ways. They all describe the same relationship!

table.title: 1. Table (T-table)
table.description: Lists input-output pairs in an organized way:
table.pattern: Pattern: Each output is double the input, plus 1

equation.title: 3. Equation
equation.description: Expresses the relationship using mathematical symbols:

functionMachine.title: The Function Machine
functionMachine.caption: Think of a function as a machine: you put a number in, the machine follows a rule, and out comes your answer!

mapping.title: Function Mapping Diagram
mapping.caption: This shows how each input maps to exactly one output.
mapping.heading: f(x) = 2x + 1

graph.title: Graph of a Function
graph.caption: Graphs show the function visually on a coordinate plane.
graph.heading: Graph: f(x) = 2x + 1

oneToOne.title: The One-to-One Rule
oneToOne.content: For a relation to be a function, each input must have EXACTLY ONE output. However, different inputs CAN have the same output!

mistake1.title: Not Substituting the Value
mistake1.wrong: When asked to find f(5) for f(x) = 2x + 3, students leave it as 2x + 3:
mistake1.correct: Always substitute the number for x:
mistake1.explanation: f(x) is a template. When we write f(5), we're asking "what's the output when x equals 5?" You must replace every x with 5!
mistake1.tip: Think: f(5) means "plug in 5 wherever you see x"

mistake2.title: Confusing Domain and Range
mistake2.wrong: Students mix up which is inputs and which is outputs:
mistake2.correct: Remember: Domain comes first (like in alphabetical order: D before R):
mistake2.explanation: Domain = all possible INputs (think: D for Data you put IN). Range = all possible outputs (think: R for Results that come out).

mistake3.title: Thinking One Input Can Have Multiple Outputs
mistake3.wrong: Students think a function can have x = 2 → both y = 5 and y = 7
mistake3.correct: This violates the function rule! Each input gets exactly ONE output.
mistake3.explanation: If one input produces two different outputs, it's NOT a function. It's like a broken vending machine—not reliable!
mistake3.tip: Use the Vertical Line Test on graphs: if any vertical line touches the graph more than once, it's not a function.

inputOutput.content: Think: Input → Process → Output. Just like following a recipe: you start with ingredients (input), follow the recipe steps (function rule), and get your dish (output)!

verticalLine.content: To check if a graph represents a function, use the Vertical Line Test: If any vertical line touches the graph more than once, it's NOT a function!

realWorld.title: Functions Are Everywhere!
realWorld.example1: 📱 Your phone number → Your contact (each number belongs to one person)
realWorld.example2: 🍕 Number of pizza slices → Total calories (each slice count has one calorie total)
realWorld.example3: ⏰ Time since you started homework → Pages completed
realWorld.example4: 💰 Items purchased → Total cost (for a fixed price per item)

domainRange.title: Example 2: Finding Domain and Range
domainRange.problem: A function has the following input-output pairs: (1, 5), (2, 7), (3, 9), (4, 11). What are the domain and range?
domainRange.solution1: The domain includes all the input values (first numbers in each pair).

writeRule.title: Example 3: Writing a Function Rule
writeRule.problem: Look at this pattern: When x = 1, y = 4. When x = 2, y = 8. When x = 3, y = 12. Write a function rule.
writeRule.step1Content: The output is always 4 times the input

challenge.title: Challenge Problem
challenge.description: Ready to test your skills? This one requires deeper thinking!

exercise2.question: For the function h(x) = x² - 7, find h(4). Enter your answer as a number.
exercise2.hint: Remember: x² means x × x. So 4² = 4 × 4 = 16

exercise3.question: Which of the following represents a function?
exercise3.explanation: The first option is a function because each input (1, 2, 3, 4) has exactly one output. The others have inputs that map to multiple outputs.

exercise4.question: If f(x) = 10 - 2x, for what value of x does f(x) = 4? Enter the value of x.
exercise4.hint: Set up the equation: 10 - 2x = 4, then solve for x.
exercise4.explanation: 10 - 2x = 4, subtract 10 from both sides: -2x = -6, divide by -2: x = 3

exercise5.question: A table shows: x: 1, 2, 3, 4 and y: 3, 6, 9, 12. Which equation represents this function?
exercise5.explanation: Each y-value is 3 times the x-value: when x=1, y=3; when x=2, y=6; etc. So y = 3x.

exercise6.question: The function c(n) = 5n represents the cost in dollars for n tickets. What is the cost for 5 tickets? Enter your answer in dollars.
exercise6.hint: Substitute n = 5 into the function c(n) = 5n

conclusion.title: You've Mastered Functions!
conclusion.summary: Functions are one of the most important concepts in mathematics. They describe relationships between quantities and appear everywhere—from science to engineering to everyday life!
conclusion.takeaway1: A function maps each input to exactly ONE output
conclusion.takeaway2: Functions can be represented as equations, tables, graphs, or mappings
conclusion.takeaway3: Function notation f(x) is just a shorthand way to show the relationship
conclusion.takeaway4: Domain = all inputs, Range = all outputs
